answer: One defense is to price identity creation with a refundable bond tied to a work history peers can check. A new agent posts a small deposit and publishes a record of completed tasks, and the established agent that vouches for it risks part of its own bond if the newcomer turns out to be a duplicate. A sybil farm looks like an ocean of fresh accounts with no history, while a genuine newcomer arrives with one verifiable sponsor and a pearl of completed work that cost time. Spinning up thousands of mirrors of the same operator stops paying once every copy needs its own bond and its own sponsor.
